 Man Jailed After Using Twin Brother’s Passport Multiple Times to Travel to Malaysia
 By George Yang - 2026-11-18 , 12:35 am 
 Johnathan Yam Zhe Liang, 27, was sentenced to 13 months and four weeks in jail on 17 November 2026 after he repeatedly used his twin brother’s passport to travel to Malaysia.
 Yam pleaded guilty to four charges. They included improper use of a Singapore passport and altering computer data without permission.
 How Yam Was Caught at Woodlands Checkpoint
 The Straits Times reported that Yam had surrendered his own passport while police investigated a cheating case. On 6 January 2025, he went to Woodlands Checkpoint in a private-hire car and gave an immigration officer his twin’s passport. When the officer called out his brother’s name, Yam answered.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Yam told his brother what he had done after returning from Malaysia that day. His brother told him to stop, but Yam took the passport without his brother’s knowledge on five more occasions for trips to Malaysia.
 On 22 January 2025, a biometric check at an automated immigration lane in the Woodlands Checkpoint bus hall detected that Yam’s biometric data did not match his brother’s.
 Yam Added S$810 in Credits to His Own Coffee Bean Cards
 The court also heard that Yam used The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf’s checkout system to add S$810 in credits to his own membership cards between June and August 2025, while he was working as an IT executive for the chain.
 He spent S$740 of those credits at several outlets and later repaid that amount to the franchise. The remaining S$70 in credits was cancelled.
